g201.text: Last time, we asked: mould on bread, or yeast for making bread? Both are fungi! Which one is useful?

g202.text: Let's find out! One slice of bread. One bag. Ten days!

g301.text: You lock in first. One finger for every point. And find the lizard!

h501.text: Are you ready? Three! Two! One! Go!

g501.text: Day one. A slice of bread goes into a bag. We seal it. It stays shut for ten days.

g602.text: Ooh, fuzzy! Let me open the bag and sniff it!

g603.text: Something is not safe. If you can spot it, cross your arms. Hold on!

g604.text: Arms crossed? One finger up! Never touch or sniff mould. The bag stays shut.

g702.text: It is not dust. It grew!

g703.text: Bread mould is a fungus that grows on bread.

g801.text: Round one. Living things need food. But nobody fed this mould! How does it get its food? One, it makes its own. Two, from the bread. Three, it needs no food. Show me with your fingers.

g803.text: Three. Nobody fed it. Maybe it needs no food?

g804.text: Two! Living things need food. And the bread is the only food in there!

g901.text: Be a spore! Shrink down. Quietly.

g902.text: You are a spore of bread mould. You float in the kitchen air.

g903.text: You land on a slice of bread.

g904.text: The bag closes. You are already inside!

g905.text: You grow thin threads into the bread.

g906.text: You make a substance. It breaks the bread down into simpler substances.

g908.text: You grow into a fuzzy patch, and make new spores.

g1001.text: The answer is two. From the bread!

g1003.text: Fungi are living things that do not make their own food. Fungi grow on another object. They produce a substance to break down the other object into simpler substances and absorb them as food.

g1101.text: A mushroom is a fungus too. The cap. The stalk. And under the cap, the gills.

g1102.text: Nice cap! Can I try it on?

g1103.text: Mushrooms have spores that are found in gills under the cap. When the wind blows, the spores are dispersed.

g1105.text: Fungi can reproduce very quickly through spores.

g1201.text: Now, the question from last time! Which fungus is useful? One, mould. Two, yeast. Show me your fingers!

g1204.text: Yeast! It makes the dough rise.

g1206.text: So are all the other fungi harmful?

g1207.text: There are some fungi that are useful, while others are harmful to us.

g1208.text: Edible mushrooms are useful since they are food for us.

g1210.text: Yeast is another useful fungus as it is commonly used in baking bread to make the dough rise.

g1211.text: Tempeh is made with a useful fungus.

g1212.text: Bread mould is an example of harmful fungi. Eating mouldy bread can cause us to fall sick.

g1301.text: Show me your score hand! More than two? You beat the Buddies. Three fingers? High five!

g1302.text: Did you spot the lizard? It was on the fridge, with the magnets. Is a lizard a fungus? Tell someone at home.

h860.text: Let's read today's key words together! Ready?

g1401.text: Day ten. The bag goes into the bin, still shut. Then we wash our hands.

g1403.text: So what is on them? Find out in Part Two!
